text:
alex_support: FYI escalated ticket from ACME-ops, production clients in their VPC started seeing TLS handshakes fail immediately after our scheduled cert rotation at 03:00 UTC. They report 502s and auth errors. Ticket: https://support.redwood.example/t/12345 :eyes:
rotator-bot: rotation completed for tenant acme-corp at 2026-03-15T03:00Z (new cert serial 0x9f3a) :white_check_mark:
acme_ops: we rolled the new cert on our side per instructions, but clients with pinned certs started failing. `curl` shows TLS error: "SSL: certificate verify failed"
alex_support: attached their debug ssh capture, they show client logs with OpenSSL verify error and fingerprint check failing. pasted output:
```
$ openssl s_client -connect api.private.acme:443 -servername api.private.acme -showcerts
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = ExampleCA, CN = ExampleRoot
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=api.private.acme
   i:/CN=ACME Intermediate
 1 s:/CN=ACME Intermediate
   i:/CN=ExampleRoot
---
---
SSL-Session:
    Protocol  : TLSv1.3
    Cipher    : TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
---
# client pinned fingerprint (expected): SHA256:AB:CD:EF:...:12
# server presented fingerprint: SHA256:12:34:56:...:98
```

mike_oncall: quick notes from packet capture — server finished handshake, but client aborted during cert-pin check. No TLS alerts from our side. Looks like the presented cert is ECDSA with P-256 key. The previous leaf cert before rotation was RSA-2048.
tara_crypto: hypothesis: ACME client is performing a strict public-key/fingerprint pin check that assumes RSA key material and compares raw SubjectPublicKeyInfo bytes (or an old SHA1 pin). Our rotation created an ECDSA leaf (ECDSA-with-SHA256) which naturally changes the fingerprint. If their client only accepts the exact fingerprint it will fail even though chain is valid. Also possible their HSM or legacy client doesn't support ECDSA signatures.
jess_csm: confirmed with customer — they have an internal policy that pins the certificate SHA1 fingerprint in their config for the app, and their client stack is an older FIPS image that omits ECDSA support. They asked us to roll back.
alex_support: mitigation applied: enabled legacy RSA fallback cert (rotator configured dual-key leaf) and forced a quick rotator re-issue for acme-corp at 03:18 UTC. rotator-bot: issued dual-cert bundle containing RSA+ECDSA variants, served RSA on clients that prefer it.
rotator-bot: quick note: dual-key workflow is experimental for a subset of tenants, flagged in config  acme-corp:dual-key=true
tara_crypto: root cause summary -> rotation changed key algorithm (RSA -> ECDSA) and customer had strict fingerprint pinning + older client without ECDSA. Action items:
- engineering: add a pre-rotation check that detects tenant pinned-fingerprints (heuristic: customer provided fingerprint or older client fingerprint seen in logs) and warn in the rotation plan (P1).
- product/ops: document dual-key/algorithm compatibility in KB and make dual-key option GA with clear rollout instructions (P2).
- support: reach out to customer with remediation steps and ask if they want forced rollback or dual-key enabled (done).
mike_oncall: also noted: add a short rollback playbook for urgent pinning break — `rotator rollback --tenant acme-corp --to-serial 0x9f2b` and a health-check endpoint to validate fingerprint post-rotation.
jess_csm: customer accepted dual-key and will update app stack in next maintenance window. They requested an RFC on safer rotation for pinned environments. I'll coordinate and set a follow-up meeting. :calendar:
alex_support: tagging @tara_crypto @mike_oncall — please include timeline estimates for the pre-rotation check and making dual-key GA. I'll update the ticket and close this support incident once KB and playbook are linked. :thumbsup:
tara_crypto: ack, will draft design doc today, estimate 3 days for prototype check + 2 weeks for production rollout behind a flag.
mike_oncall: ack, will add rollback commands to runbook and add an automated fingerprint validator in the healthcheck endpoint (ETA 4 days).
acme_ops: thanks team — appreciate the fast response. we'll keep dual-key for now and schedule stack upgrade.
alex_support: closing note: this thread for the ticket; follow-ups should be in #eng-runtime RFC thread once design doc ready.
